findings.reason: the mechanism must be narrowed to records whose `review_run_id` names the promoting run (the measured misnamed record carries it), which satisfies all three cases without refiling a sibling's copy over a stored disposition.
findings.text: filing "by its content as well as by its name" is scoped to any record naming the reviewed run, but the staging store keys a text review by reviewed run and head only, so promoting one review run re-files a *sibling or superseded* review run's delivered copy over the record currently in that slot, discarding any `finding_dispositions` written there and letting directory order decide which of several reviews of one head is current — the plan's own evidence exhibits it: that `review-records/` holds records from review runs `r-20261024T210701164481` and `r-20261024T214207355407`, and the store's single `.at-d6ee413e2ca9` record now carries the later run's content, which a content scan for the earlier run would overwrite
